Using the current WHATWG URL Standard, an `https:` URL is normalized in these ways during parse/serialize. All claims below are supported directly by the standard unless labeled `Inference`. Sources: <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-parsing>, <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#idna>, <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous>, <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing>, <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes>, <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-serializing>.

**Supported fact**

For a Unicode hostname in an `https:` URL, the host parser first percent-decodes the host input, UTF-8-decodes that result, and then runs the domain parser with `beStrict = false`. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-parsing>

The domain parser lowercases an all-ASCII domain, and for a non-ASCII domain it runs Unicode ToASCII with UTS #46 settings; the result must be non-empty and contain no forbidden domain code points. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#idna>

A host serializer returns an ASCII string, and the spec’s own parse-serialize example shows `faß.example` becoming `xn--fa-hia.example`. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-serializing>

`https` is a special scheme whose default port is `443`. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous>

When the parser reads a port, it stores `null` instead of the numeric port if the parsed port equals the scheme’s default port. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing>

When a URL is serialized, the port is emitted only if the stored port is non-null. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-serializing>

A single-dot path segment is `"."` or an ASCII-case-insensitive match for `"%2e"`. A double-dot path segment is `".."`, `".%2e"`, `"%2e."`, or `"%2e%2e"` with ASCII-case-insensitive matching. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous>

In path state, a double-dot segment causes the parser to shorten the URL’s path, and a single-dot segment is not appended as a normal segment. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing>

When the parser encounters `#`, it creates an empty fragment and switches to fragment state. In fragment state, code points are UTF-8-percent-encoded using the fragment percent-encode set and appended to the fragment. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes>

On serialization, `#` is added back only if the URL’s fragment is non-null. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-serializing>

In path state, non-URL code points other than `%` cause a validation error, malformed `%` escapes cause a validation error, and otherwise each code point is UTF-8-percent-encoded using the path percent-encode set and appended to the path buffer. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes>

The standard also says that code points above U+007F are converted to percent-encoded bytes by the URL parser. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous>

**Inference**

Because the path parser appends valid `%` escapes through the normal path-state logic, and because the percent-encode sets used by the URL parser do not encode `%`, valid percent-encoded path bytes are preserved rather than percent-decoded during parsing. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes>

Because default `https` port `443` is converted to stored `null`, and serialization omits null ports, an explicit `:443` disappears from the serialized URL. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-serializing>

Because single-dot and double-dot segments are recognized even in `%2e` forms, those dot segments are normalized away during parsing rather than preserved literally as ordinary path segments. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing>

**Uncertainty / lack of good evidence**

I found no direct statement in the standard that valid percent-encoded path bytes are hex-case-normalized during parsing, and the cited parsing/serialization rules do not show such a rewrite. That makes “no hex-case normalization of already-valid path escapes” a cautious inference, not a directly stated rule. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-serializing>

**Bottom line**

For an `https:` URL, the standard normalizes the host to an ASCII domain form via IDNA processing, drops an explicit default port `:443`, resolves dot segments in the path, stores the fragment separately from `#` while percent-encoding fragment code points as needed, and percent-encodes path code points as needed without directly stating that already-valid percent-encoded path bytes are decoded or hex-case-normalized. <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#host-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#idna> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-miscellaneous> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-parsing> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#percent-encoded-bytes> <https://url.spec.whatwg.org/#url-serializing>
